title: How silicon-chip technology is being re-engineered for quantum computing
excerpt: Two demonstrations of silicon-based quantum processors tackle the engineering challenges of building scalable quantum computers.

• NEWS AND VIEWS
  • 29 July 2026

Two demonstrations of silicon-based quantum processors tackle the engineering challenges of building scalable quantum computers.

By

  1. Natalia Ares

    1. Natalia Ares is in the Department of Engineering Science, University of Oxford, Oxford OX1 3PJ, UK.

Decades of development in semiconductor technology mean that conventional computers now contain billions of transistors, packed onto tiny silicon chips. Silicon transistors are cheap, fast and reliable, and there is considerable interest in applying this technology to quantum computers. A quantum computer based on silicon microchips could in theory perform, in hours, complex calculations that would take today’s best classical (non-quantum) computers longer than the lifetime of the Universe. Now, two papers in Nature take on the challenge of connecting and controlling ‘quantum transistors’ in silicon quantum processors. Undseth et al.1 report a quantum processor with reconfigurable long-range connectivity, whereas the HRL team2 describes a processing unit controlled by electronics that operate at cryogenic temperatures, close to the temperature of the quantum processor itself.

Nature 655, 1141-1142 (2026)

• 新闻和观点

硅基量子处理器的两个演示解决了构建可扩展量子计算机的工程挑战。

By

  1. Natalia Ares Natalia Ares 就职于牛津大学工程科学系，地址：Oxford OX1 3PJ，UK。

半导体技术数十年的发展意味着传统计算机现在包含数十亿个晶体管，这些晶体管封装在微小的硅芯片上。 硅晶体管便宜、快速且可靠，人们对将该技术应用于量子计算机抱有很大兴趣。 理论上，基于硅微芯片的量子计算机可以在数小时内执行复杂的计算，而当今最好的经典（非量子）计算机所需的时间比宇宙的寿命还要长。 现在，《自然》杂志上的两篇论文探讨了连接和控制硅量子处理器中“量子晶体管”的挑战。 Undseth 等人 1 报告了一种具有可重新配置远程连接的量子处理器，而 HRL 团队 2 描述了一种由电子设备控制的处理单元，该处理单元在接近量子处理器本身温度的低温下运行。

Nature 655, 1141-1142 (2026)

doi：https://doi.org/10.1038/d41586-026-02124-0
